issues.body: is_status_evaluator_artifact() excludes every check run named `ci-summary status`, without verifying that it belongs to the trusted ci-summary-status workflow or SELF_RUN_ID. A same-repository PR controls its workflow job names and can give a failing or pending job this exact name. run_gate() will then remove that real leg from the sibling set, so the currently required `ci-summary / gate` can report success despite the hidden failure. The new unit test explicitly validates name-only exclusion but never tests provenance, making this a merge-authorization bypass rather than merely an observational-stage concern.
issues.fix_hint: Identify evaluator artifacts using trusted run provenance (for example, resolve the check to its workflow run and require the exact default-branch workflow identity/event in addition to the job name), or exclude only the anchored evaluator run IDs known to the invocation. Add an adversarial test where a pull-request workflow creates a same-named failing job and prove it still gates, while genuine evaluator runs are excluded.
issues.title: Name-only artifact exclusion lets PR-controlled jobs bypass the required gate

issues.body: The workflow omits `workflow_run.workflows` and acknowledges that whether this subscribes to all workflows is unverified. GitHub's workflow_run configuration uses `workflows` to specify the upstream workflow(s); shipping an event-driven transport with no established upstream means the workflow may be invalid or never fire. This defeats stage 1 itself: there will be no status or parity evidence to observe, and the repository test only searches YAML text rather than validating the workflow against GitHub's schema/runtime semantics.
issues.fix_hint: Use a GitHub-supported trigger configuration with explicitly established semantics and add schema validation. If enumerating workflows is unacceptable, redesign the event source before merging rather than shipping a known silent-failure assumption; document and test how newly added workflows are included.
issues.title: workflow_run trigger has no upstream workflow selector

verdict.summary: The slotless evaluator is not safe or complete as implemented. Its artifact exclusion trusts only a caller-controlled check-run name, allowing a PR workflow to hide a failing job from both the existing required gate and the proposed status. In addition, the new workflow intentionally omits the workflow_run workflows selector even though that selector identifies the upstream workflows; the submitted configuration therefore lacks a valid, demonstrated event source and may never publish the observational status. The tests encode both assumptions rather than exercising GitHub provenance/configuration semantics.
